public_body: Wayland Town Center Green Advisory Committee
overall: The AG found the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to provide or timely create minutes and by failing to respond to the complaint, declined the untimely notice claim, and found no violation on draft minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Committee's meeting notices for seven 2012 meetings did not list topics specifically enough to inform the public.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore decline to investigate whether the notices stated topics with sufficient specificity because the complaint was filed with the Committee more than 30 days after these meetings.

allegations.summary: Complainant requested all Committee minutes on September 14, 2012 and alleged they were not provided within 10 days.
allegations.key_passage: Following our review, we find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by either failing to provide its meeting minutes within 10 days of a request, or by failing to create minutes in a timely manner.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the August 2, 2012 minutes were defective because they did not list the documents used at the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: However, we note that these are only draft minutes and have not been approved by the Committee. Therefore, we do not find a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: The Committee did not respond to the complaint or the AG despite a granted extension to November 30, 2012.
allegations.key_passage: Finally, we find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to respond to this complaint, despite being granted additional time to do so.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
Committee members must view the Attorney General's Open Meeting Law training video and certify in writing to the AG's office within 30 days of receipt that all members have done so.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law. We also order the Committee to view the video of the Open Meeting Law training available on the Attorney General's Open Meeting Law website, and certify, in writing to this office, within thirty (30) days of receipt of this determination that all members have done so.
